title: Ramayana: Part One passes Rs 500 crore in India in its first week, trackers estimate
dek: Estimates of the worldwide gross range from about Rs 918 crore to Rs 935 crore. The makers have not released official figures.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part One earned about Rs 511 crore net in India in its first seven days, according to estimates by one box-office tracker. The makers have not published official figures, and trackers' estimates differ.

The same tracker put the film's first-week worldwide gross at about Rs 935 crore, including about Rs 324 crore from overseas. Another trade tracker's lower estimate of the India net for the first seven days works out to about Rs 490 crore, and it puts the worldwide gross, including part of the eighth day, at about Rs 918 crore.

The film, which opened on 5 November, had its biggest day on Monday, 9 November, during the Diwali holidays, with about Rs 107.5 crore net, by that tracker's estimate. Trade analysts said the Hindi version set records for a Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday collection. The Hindi version alone earned about Rs 409.56 crore net in its first week, trade analyst Taran Adarsh said.

The film is the first of two parts, produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, with music by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman. Its second weekend, from 13 to 15 November, is likely to decide whether it crosses Rs 1,000 crore worldwide.
